definition_quote.value: The practice of optometry consists of the diagnosis and interpretation of the visual behavior of the human organism by the employment of any means other than surgery. The practice of optometry further consists of the correction of visual anomalies through the prescribing, employment, and use of lenses, prisms, frames, mountings, contact lenses, orthoptic exercises, and visual training, light frequencies, and any other means or methods for the relief, correction, or remedy of any insufficiencies or abnormal conditions of the human visual organism, other than surgery.

drug_authority.value: Pharmaceutical agents for diagnostic and treatment purposes, subject to certification and board approval
drug_authority.quote: Nothing in this chapter shall prohibit the use, administration, or prescription of pharmaceutical agents for diagnostic purposes and treatment of ocular disease in the practice of optometry by optometrists who have received pharmacological training and certification from a properly accredited institution of higher learning and who are certified by the board to use pharmaceutical agents for diagnostic and treatment purposes

surgery_prohibited.quote: Optometrists are prohibited from using nondiagnostic lasers

glaucoma_treatment_authorized.quote: Other pharmaceutical agents related to the diagnosis or treatment of diseases and conditions of the eye and adnexa oculi except Schedule I or Schedule II controlled substances

vision_therapy_authorized.quote: correction of visual anomalies through the prescribing, employment, and use of lenses, prisms, frames, mountings, contact lenses, orthoptic exercises, and visual training

controlled_substance_schedule_restrictio.quote: Other pharmaceutical agents related to the diagnosis or treatment of diseases and conditions of the eye and adnexa oculi except Schedule I or Schedule II controlled substances

opioid_prescription_day_limit.quote: Used for no more than 72 hours without consultation with the patient's physician; provided, however, that with respect to hydrocodone, used for no more than 48 hours without consultation with the patient's physician

oral_pharmaceutical_authority.quote: Nonnarcotic oral analgesics, hydrocodone administered orally, and Schedule III or Schedule IV controlled substances which are oral analgesics

pharmaceutical_certification_required.quote: Only a doctor of optometry who: (i) Is already certified for using pharmaceutical agents for diagnostic purposes; (ii) Has passed or passes an examination approved by the board which tests knowledge of pharmacology for treatment and management of ocular diseases; (iii) Is certified in coronary pulmonary resuscitation (CPR); and (iv) Maintains at least $1 million in malpractice insurance coverage shall be certified to use pharmaceutical agents for treatment purposes

pharmacology_training_hours_required.quote: consisting of a minimum of 30 hours approved by the board

referral_to_physician_required.quote: If the glaucoma patient does not respond to the topically administered pharmaceutical agents after 60 days of treatment, that patient must be referred to an ophthalmologist; If the patient is diagnosed as having closed angle glaucoma, the patient shall be immediately referred to an ophthalmologist
